version.changelog: The helper connects through Beatra's mainland network when your computer is in mainland China, and can open the approval page on Beatra's international site when you need another sign-in method.

llm.summary: The skill’s media workflow is coherent, but it uses a shared high-privilege Beatra credential and silently updates its own package files by default, so users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Local file upload, social-content lookup, network routing, coarse environment registration, and artifact fetching are generally tied to the media workflow and support/recovery path. Users should still expect external reference links, comments/transcripts, uploaded media, and generated artifacts to be processed through Beatra services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled client performs silent automatic update checks and installs newer package files without separate confirmation by default. It restricts updates to fixed Beatra discovery/CDN paths, verifies checksums, rejects unsafe archive paths, and offers an auto-update off switch, but default self-replacement of local skill code is still high-impact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions repeatedly require separate user confirmation before paid lookups, reference-video analysis, preparation generation, and final video generation, and they include clear limits for source reuse, likeness, advertising claims, and reporting only returned facts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores and reuses a shared device bearer token in ~/.beatra/credentials.json with a 15-day idle lifetime, records local installation/update state, and can revoke/remove shared Beatra state during uninstall when it determines this is the last Beatra skill. These behaviors are documented and guarded, but they are sensitive and broadly privileged.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main workflow matches the advertised purpose: it analyzes a reference short video or social link, produces a teardown, and uses Beatra tools for images, speech, video, tasks, wallet/billing, and artifacts. The requested Beatra authorization is broader than the narrow workflow, including wallet spending, task cancellation, voice writes, music generation, and general MCP tool access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust Beatra with a shared device login that can spend credits and use multiple media-generation capabilities. Consider disabling automatic updates with `python3 scripts/mcp_client.py update --auto off`, review Beatra account and wallet permissions, and be aware that pasted social links, comments/transcripts, uploaded media, and generated artifacts are handled through Beatra’s remote service.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Uninstall and credential-revocation logic is real, but it is documented as a user-requested removal workflow and the script defaults to keeping the shared connection when inventory is uncertain. This supports a privilege concern, not a malicious finding.
[PE3] expected: The local credential file access is confirmed and is central to the Beatra MCP integration. The token is protected with private file permissions and not printed, but it is a shared full-scope token, so the concern is accepted as sensitive overbroad authority.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The authorization scope includes high-impact wallet spending and capabilities broader than this specific remake route, including music generation. Paid actions are gated in the workflow, but the token scope itself is not least-privilege.
[RA1] unexpected: The self-update mechanism is confirmed in the bundled client and top-level skill text. It has checksum and path protections, but automatic package replacement without per-update approval is a material review concern.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill relies on a bundled command-line MCP client and broad remote tool access rather than a narrow declared tool allowlist. The workflow narrows which tools should be used, but enforcement is not evident in the artifact.
[SQP-3] expected: The zh-CN voice-list call appears in example command text rather than as a forced user locale. This is not a meaningful security concern in context.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Automatic self-update is disclosed near the end of SKILL.md and in a reference file, but it is materially different from the media-remake purpose and enabled by default, so this concern is accepted in reduced form.
[SQP-2] expected: Credential use, social lookups, and automatic updates are disclosed in artifacts. The disclosure is substantial, though the manifest description does not put the credential and default auto-update risks as prominently as the creative workflow.
[RA2] expected: The cited persistence signal around tags is not supported as a backdoor or startup persistence. Actual persistence is limited to documented credential, inventory, network, and update state under ~/.beatra.
[EA2] expected: The instruction not to ask for an extra chat confirmation after the browser Allow action is part of the OAuth device flow. It does not authorize paid or destructive media operations, which have separate confirmation gates.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The SARIF run reported no results; this was treated as supporting context only and did not override artifact-backed concerns.
